facts.fact: Nantucket lightship baskets began aboard the lightship stationed at the Nantucket shoals (station from 1854, baskets from the 1860s); production aboard ended about 1900 and the craft went on on the island. Rattan cane and weavers over staves, a solid wooden base, a wooden bail riveted to the rim; purse baskets with a lid; ivory whale lid ornaments from the 1940s.
The club's holes carry nautical names (from OpenStreetMap's hole names: 1 Outward Bound, 7 Cross Rip, 8 Come About, 9 Gray Lady, 18 Thar She Blows).
Cross Rip was a lightship station in Nantucket Sound.
Highland Links already uses a lighthouse; Sankaty Head Light stands beside the course.

concepts.name: The Lightship Basket
concepts.rationale: Nantucket's own craft instead of the lighthouse every Sankaty picture shows (and Highland Links already has): a lidded lightship basket with an ivory sperm whale on the lid, for the island's whaling past and the club's nautical hole names.
concepts.symbolism: The basket: the island and its lightships; the whale: Nantucket whaling.
concepts.interpretation: The link to the golf club is through the island and the hole names, not a documented club tradition.
concepts.strengths: Unique to Nantucket; reads as a basket at 32 px; warm colours stand out from the green card.
concepts.tradeoffs: The whale is small at 1x (a pale shape with an eye and flukes).
